\title{Measuring and Reducing the Cross-Dataset Generalisation Gap\\
in Audio-Visual Deepfake Detection}

\author{
\IEEEauthorblockN{Samrender Singh Saini}
\IEEEauthorblockA{\textit{Independent project}}
}

\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
% Lead with the gap. "Do not oversell" is a
% structural instruction, not a stylistic one: the measured failure is the
% contribution, and burying it would make the paper less useful, not more.
Deepfake detectors routinely report above 95\% accuracy on the dataset they
were trained on, and far less on forgeries produced by methods they have not
seen. We quantify that gap under a strict protocol in which the decision
threshold is fixed on the source-domain validation split and each target set is
evaluated exactly once. \todo{headline gap} We then reduce it with three
mechanisms that do not depend on any single generator's artefacts: self-blended
images, which synthesise training fakes from real frames alone; an
audio-visual synchrony encoder trained contrastively on real video only; and
degradation augmentation. \todo{recovered gap} Because accuracy in this regime
does not support a binary verdict, the system additionally calibrates its
probabilities, abstains through a conformal band, and flags inputs unlike its
training distribution; we report risk--coverage behaviour alongside accuracy.
\end{abstract}

\begin{IEEEkeywords}
deepfake detection, cross-dataset generalisation, audio-visual learning,
selective prediction, calibration
\end{IEEEkeywords}
